changes: Added an optional advisory PhaseAuthorityWarning to handoff packs. createHandoffPack now resolves story authority (resolveStoryAuthority) and, when a linked worktree's authoritative phase differs from the packed main-mirror phase, attaches a warning rendered by handoff_create and handoff_inspect (text + json). The field lives outside HandoffPackHashInput so packHash is byte-stable; recoveryPoint.phase semantics are unchanged; resolver failure is caught and yields no warning.
usage: Run `lattice handoff_create --storyId=<id> --fromHost=<a> --toHost=<b>`; if the story is under active worktree development at a phase ahead of the main mirror, output shows `⚠ phaseAuthority (ahead): ...`. `lattice handoff_inspect --file=<pack>` shows the same line. No warning for in-sync or no-worktree stories.
expectedOutcome: handoff_create/inspect emit a clear phase-authority warning when the worktree is ahead of the packed mirror phase, and stay silent otherwise; packHash and recoveryPoint.phase unchanged.
actualTranscript: Live on B-4e06 (worktree DEV vs mirror INIT_CHECK): handoff_create printed '⚠ phaseAuthority (ahead): Authoritative worktree phase DEV is ahead of the packed mirror phase INIT_CHECK...'; JSON carried the structured phaseAuthorityWarning; recoveryPoint.phase stayed INIT_CHECK. B-decb (no worktree): 0 warning lines. Smoke 6/6 PASS; tsc clean; lattice validate allPass.
outcomeDiff: No diff — every scenario matched the PLAN expectation (see evidence/transcript-diff.md).
limitations: The live worktree-ahead path through createHandoffPack is covered by manual evidence on B-4e06 rather than the hermetic smoke (which uses a no-worktree temp repo for the no-warning case); the warning logic itself is fully unit-covered (ahead/in-sync/no-worktree/divergent + render + hash stability).
pitfalls: The warning is advisory only: it does NOT change recoveryPoint.phase or baseSha (still main HEAD), so the resuming host must read the live worktree to continue from the true phase. Do not add phaseAuthorityWarning to HandoffPackHashInput — that would break packHash stability and existing handoff fixtures.
